guide.rules.sudoku.goal: Fill the grid with the numbers 1 to 9.
guide.rules.sudoku.1: Every row holds each number 1–9 exactly once.
guide.rules.sudoku.2: Every column holds each number 1–9 exactly once.
guide.rules.sudoku.3: Every 3×3 box holds each number 1–9 exactly once.
guide.rules.sudoku.4: The given numbers cannot be changed; a good puzzle has exactly one solution.
guide.rules.kakuro.goal: Fill the white cells with the numbers 1 to 9.
guide.rules.kakuro.1: A clue gives the sum of the run of white cells to its right (across) or below it (down).
guide.rules.kakuro.2: The cells of a run add up to its clue.
guide.rules.kakuro.3: A number appears at most once in a run.
guide.rules.futoshiki.goal: Fill the N×N grid with the numbers 1 to N.
guide.rules.futoshiki.1: Every row and every column holds each number 1–N exactly once.
guide.rules.futoshiki.2: A < or > sign between two cells says which of the two is smaller.
guide.rules.jidoku.goal: Fill the grid with the numbers 1 to 9.
guide.rules.jidoku.1: As in Sudoku, every row, column and 3×3 box holds each number 1–9 exactly once.
guide.rules.jidoku.2: There are usually no given numbers: the clues are < and > signs between neighbouring cells of a box, drawn as a bent edge that points to the smaller cell.
guide.rules.sumbrero.goal: Fill every hexagon with a number from the puzzle’s range.
guide.rules.sumbrero.1: Lines of hexagons run in three directions: straight down, down-right and up-right.
guide.rules.sumbrero.2: A clue gives the sum of its line: the hexagons of the line add up to it.
guide.rules.sumbrero.3: A number appears at most once in a line with a clue.
guide.rules.nonogram.goal: Colour the cells to reveal a picture.
guide.rules.nonogram.1: The clue of a row or column lists the lengths of its blocks of filled cells, in order.
guide.rules.nonogram.2: Blocks of the same colour have at least one blank cell between them; blocks of different colours may touch.
guide.rules.nonogram.3: All other cells are blank. With several colours, a clue’s colour is the colour of its block.
guide.technique.nakedSingle.name: Naked single
guide.technique.nakedSingle.summary: A cell with only one candidate left gets that value.
guide.technique.nakedSingle.step1: Look at the values the cell’s groups already hold: none of them can go in the cell.
guide.technique.nakedSingle.step2: When all values but one are ruled out, the last one is the cell’s value.
guide.technique.nakedSingle.example: A Sudoku cell whose row, column and box together hold 1–8 must be 9.
guide.technique.hiddenSingle.name: Hidden single
guide.technique.hiddenSingle.summary: A value that fits in only one cell of a group goes in that cell.
guide.technique.hiddenSingle.step1: Pick a group that needs every value once (a row, column or box) and a value it still misses.
guide.technique.hiddenSingle.step2: Rule out every open cell that cannot hold it: if one cell is left, the value goes there, even when that cell has other candidates too.
guide.technique.hiddenSingle.example: If 4 is missing from a row and the other open cells of the row all see a 4, the 4 goes in the last cell.
guide.technique.hiddenSingle.caption: The row misses 2, 4, 8 and 9; only the marked cell can hold 4.
guide.technique.elimination.name: Elimination
guide.technique.elimination.summary: A placed value is removed from the candidates of the cells that share a group with it.
guide.technique.elimination.step1: When a value is placed, no other cell of its groups can hold it.
guide.technique.elimination.step2: Removing it from those cells is the basis of the other techniques; with notes, cross it off as you go.
guide.technique.nakedSubset.name: Naked pair, triple, …
guide.technique.nakedSubset.summary: k cells of a group that share only k candidates take those values between them.
guide.technique.nakedSubset.step1: Find two cells of a group with the same two candidates (or three cells with three candidates between them, and so on).
guide.technique.nakedSubset.step2: Those values must go in those cells, so remove them from the other cells of the group.
guide.technique.nakedSubset.example: Two cells of a row with candidates {2, 7}: no other cell of the row can be 2 or 7.
guide.technique.nakedSubset.caption: The marked cells hold 2 and 7 between them, so the other cells of the row lose 2 and 7.
guide.technique.hiddenSubset.name: Hidden pair, triple, …
guide.technique.hiddenSubset.summary: k values that fit in only the same k cells of a group fill those cells.
guide.technique.hiddenSubset.step1: Find two values that a group still needs and that fit in the same two cells only (or three values in three cells, and so on).
guide.technique.hiddenSubset.step2: Those cells hold exactly those values, so their other candidates go.
guide.technique.hiddenSubset.example: If 3 and 8 can only go in the same two cells of a box, those cells are {3, 8}.
guide.technique.hiddenSubset.caption: 3 and 8 fit only in the marked cells of the row, so those cells lose their other candidates.
guide.technique.intersection.name: Pointing and box-line
guide.technique.intersection.summary: When a value of one group can only go where it overlaps another group, the rest of the other group loses it.
guide.technique.intersection.step1: Pointing: in a box, a value fits only in cells of one row (or column). It must go in that row there, so the row’s cells outside the box lose it.
guide.technique.intersection.step2: Box-line: in a row (or column), a value fits only in cells of one box. It must go in the box there, so the box’s other cells lose it.
guide.technique.intersection.caption: In the left box, 4 fits only in the top row, so the rest of the top row loses 4.
guide.technique.xWing.name: X-Wing
guide.technique.xWing.summary: A value that fits in the same two columns of two rows is in those columns there.
guide.technique.xWing.step1: Find two rows where a value fits in exactly two cells, and the cells are in the same two columns.
guide.technique.xWing.step2: The value goes in one corner of the rectangle in each row, so it takes both columns: the other cells of those columns lose it.
guide.technique.xWing.step3: The same works with rows and columns swapped.
guide.technique.xWing.caption: Rows 1 and 4 hold 7 only in columns 2 and 5, so the other cells of those columns lose 7.
guide.technique.swordfish.name: Swordfish
guide.technique.swordfish.summary: The X-Wing with three rows and three columns.
guide.technique.swordfish.step1: Find three rows where a value fits only in cells of the same three columns (two or three cells per row).
guide.technique.swordfish.step2: The value takes one cell of each of those columns in those rows, so the other cells of the columns lose it.
guide.technique.jellyfish.name: Jellyfish
guide.technique.jellyfish.summary: The X-Wing with four rows and four columns.
guide.technique.jellyfish.step1: Find four rows where a value fits only in cells of the same four columns.
guide.technique.jellyfish.step2: The other cells of those four columns lose the value.
guide.technique.sumCombinations.name: Sum combinations
guide.technique.sumCombinations.summary: Only values that are part of a combination adding up to the total can go in a line.
guide.technique.sumCombinations.step1: List the sets of different values that add up to the total with the right number of cells; subtract the values already placed.
guide.technique.sumCombinations.step2: A value that is in none of those sets cannot go in the line. Some totals have only one set: 3 in two cells is 1 + 2, 17 in two cells is 8 + 9.
guide.technique.sumCombinations.step3: Where two lines cross, the cell can only hold values that fit both.
guide.technique.sumCombinations.example: A line of two cells adding up to 4 is 1 + 3 (2 + 2 repeats a value), so neither cell can be 2.
guide.technique.inequality.name: Inequalities
guide.technique.inequality.summary: A cell that must be smaller than another cannot hold the largest values, and the larger cell not the smallest.
guide.technique.inequality.step1: The smaller cell must be below the largest candidate of the larger cell, the larger cell above the smallest candidate of the smaller one.
guide.technique.inequality.step2: Follow chains: in a < b < c, a is at most N − 2 and c at least 3.
guide.technique.inequality.example: If b < c and c can only be 3 or 5, b can be at most 4.
guide.technique.wholeLine.name: Whole line
guide.technique.wholeLine.summary: A line without blocks is all blank, and blocks that need the whole line fill it.
guide.technique.wholeLine.step1: Add up the blocks and the gaps they need (one blank between blocks of the same colour).
guide.technique.wholeLine.step2: If that is the length of the line, there is only one way to place them; a 0 clue means the whole line is blank.
guide.technique.wholeLine.example: Clue 3 2 in a line of 6: 3 + 1 + 2 = 6, so the line is ■■■□■■.
guide.technique.wholeLine.caption: The blocks and the gap between them need all six cells.
guide.technique.overlap.name: Overlap
guide.technique.overlap.summary: Cells that a block covers wherever it goes are that block’s colour.
guide.technique.overlap.step1: Push a block as far to the start as it can go, then as far to the end.
guide.technique.overlap.step2: The cells it covers in both positions are filled, wherever it ends up.
guide.technique.overlap.example: A block of 7 in a line of 10 can start at cell 1 to 4: cells 4–7 are always covered.
guide.technique.overlap.caption: Wherever the block of 7 goes, it covers the middle four cells.
guide.technique.reach.name: Out of reach
guide.technique.reach.summary: A cell that no block of a colour can reach is not that colour.
guide.technique.reach.step1: For each block, work out the first and last cell it can cover.
guide.technique.reach.step2: Cells outside the reach of every block of a colour cannot be that colour; with one colour they are blank.
guide.technique.placements.name: All placements
guide.technique.placements.summary: A colour that a cell has in no placement of the blocks that fits the known cells is ruled out.
guide.technique.placements.step1: Try every way to place the blocks of a line that agrees with the cells you know.
guide.technique.placements.step2: A cell that has the same colour in all of them gets that colour; a colour it never gets is ruled out.
guide.technique.guess.name: Guessing
guide.technique.guess.summary: When nothing follows from the rules, try a value and see whether it leads to a contradiction.
guide.technique.guess.step1: Pick a cell with few candidates and assume one of them.
guide.technique.guess.step2: Carry on solving; if a rule breaks, the guess was wrong, so go back and remove that candidate. The app only guesses with Allow guessing on.
